newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia says 1996 real deficit was 17 bln.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia says 1996 real deficit was 17 bln.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's real deficit in 1996 stood at 17 billion riyals ($4.5 billion), down from a projected 18.5 billion riyals, a Finance Ministry statement said on Monday.
The statement said real spending in 1996 was 194 billion riyals, up from the projected 150 billion riyals. Real revenue stood at 177 billion riyals up from the 131.5 billion forecast.

It said the rise in expenditure was "mainly due to the measures taken in the year to pay the dues of farmers, contractors and companies...where seven billion riyals were paid to farmers and more than 15 billion riyals were paid to individuals, contractors, importers and other companies."
"These measures had boosted confidence in the national economy and were also reflected in the development the kigndom is witnessing in different sectors," the statement said.

It was issued by the official media after the announcement of the 1997 budget, which forecast a 17 billion riyals deficit. The arrears had been accumulating since the 1990-91 Gulf war mostly due to the high costs of the war and the weak oil prices, but in the past year, cash payments have been made and special bonds issued to meet the dues.
Economists in the kingdom say the government has started meeting current payments on time.
